mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is observed in historical data without requiring additional regime conditions.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong aggregate demand, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. The effect is multiplicative and requires both series to be rising.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS growth > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS growth exceed 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions characterized by low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and strong labor market growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overheating and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. This effect is consistent across business cycles.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of months where INDPRO increases, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal a tightening monetary policy cycle that reduces real equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. The effect is multiplicative and requires both series to be rising.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth > 0.3% MoM and FEDFUNDS growth > 0.1% MoM
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS growth exceed their thresholds, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of supply chain disruption (INDPRO growth < 0.2% MoM), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced corporate profitability, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 days. This effect is most pronounced during high inflation regimes.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO growth is below 0.2% MoM, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.03.
